note.explanation: Use the empirical formula and the molar mass to find the molecular formula. First divide the molar mass by the empirical formula mass to find n. Then multiply every subscript in the empirical formula by n.
note.simple: The empirical formula is the simplest ratio. The molecular formula tells the actual number of each kind of atom. Find how many times the simplest formula fits, then multiply its subscripts by that number.
note.checkQuestion: The empirical formula is CH2O and the molar mass is 90 g mol⁻¹. What is the molecular formula?
note.title: Finding a molecular formula
steps: Calculate n = molar mass / empirical formula mass.
Multiply each subscript in the empirical formula by n.
note.answer: Molecular formula = n(Empirical Formula), where n = Molar Mass / Empirical Formula mass.

written.text: Q1.1. Different compounds will never have the same molecule formula but they can have the same empirical formula. Explain
written.finalAnswer: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms, so different molecular formulas can reduce to the same empirical formula. For example, C2H4 and C3H6 both have empirical formula CH2.

rubric.why: The meaning of empirical formula explains why different formulas can reduce to one ratio.

written.text: Q1.2. The chemical formula for sand is SiO₂ but the sand does not exist in the form of discrete molecules like H₂O. How has its formula been determined keeping in view its structure?
written.finalAnswer: SiO2 is the empirical formula for the repeating structure of sand: silicon and oxygen atoms occur in a 1:2 ratio. It represents the simplest ratio of atoms, not a discrete SiO2 molecule.

rubric.why: The ratio of atoms in the structure determines the formula.
rubric.how: State that the ratio is 1:2.

rubric.why: A repeating solid structure is represented by its simplest ratio.
rubric.how: Explain that it gives the simplest ratio of atoms.

rubric.why: The answer should relate the formula to sand's extended structure.
rubric.how: Explain that the atoms form a repeating structure rather than separate molecules.

rubric.why: The correct formula completes the response.
rubric.how: Give SiO₂ as the simplest ratio formula.

modelAnswer: Sand has a repeating structure rather than separate SiO₂ molecules.
In this structure, silicon and oxygen atoms are present in the ratio 1:2.
The formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of these atoms.
Therefore, the formula is SiO₂.

explain.title: Empirical formula
explain.body: The empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. For example, CH₂O is a simplest ratio.

explain.title: Molecular formula
explain.body: The molecular formula tells how many atoms of each element are present in a molecule. The textbook states: “Molecular formula of a compound can be found out if we know its empirical formula.”

explain.title: Find the multiplier
explain.body: Use the textbook relationship: “Molecular formula = n (Empirical Formula)” and “Where n = Molar Mass / Empirical Formula mass”. Find the empirical formula mass, divide the molar mass by it, and multiply each subscript by n.

explain.title: When n equals one
explain.body: If n is one, the molecular formula is the same as the empirical formula.

mistakes: Using the molar mass as n instead of dividing it by the empirical formula mass.
Calculating the empirical formula mass incorrectly; include every atom in the empirical formula.
Multiplying only one subscript instead of multiplying every subscript by n.
Giving the empirical formula instead of expanding it to the molecular formula when n is greater than one.
